newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Higher priorities than NZ Govt building - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Higher priorities than NZ Govt building - Peters.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters said on Thursday the New Zealand government had higher priorities than a planned NZ$94 million ministerial building.
Peters told journalists there were critical areas of social need that should be addressed first, Radio New Zealand reported.

Cabinet approved the new building last week, but several government MPs have expressed concern at the impact on public opinion of the spending at a time when other areas of outlay are being kept under tight control.
Richard Prebble, leader of the free market Act party, said he planned to introduce a private members bill to try and stop the building, which he described as "extravagant".
Peters said he thought that both MPs and the Government should be making economies.
His comments on the building came as he responded with a vigorous denial to comments in an editorial in the Australian Financial Review that New Zealand's fiscal spending discipline risked slippage.
Peters said in a statement that talk of some form of spending blowout was "unsubstantiated scaremongering".
A spokesman for Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Tuesday the spending on the new building was being reviewed but it was likely to go ahead.
